title: Destructuring Declarations
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of destructuring declarations using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates destructuring declarations.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Destructuring Declarations** as part of **Advanced Properties and Class Modeling**. Apply destructuring declarations by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—Destructuring Pairs and Triples, Destructuring Data Classes, Destructuring in Loops and Lambdas—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with destructuring pairs and triples. Then compare it with destructuring data classes. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Destructuring Pairs and Triples
items.text: Destructuring Pairs and Triples is one part of destructuring declarations. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Destructuring Data Classes
items.text: Destructuring Data Classes should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

items.title: Destructuring in Loops and Lambdas
items.text: Destructuring in Loops and Lambdas describes how behavior is declared, passed, or composed. Make inputs and return types clear, keep side effects visible, and use a small call-site example to judge readability.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
